chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Shu'ayb al-Aqraqufi, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both. He said:
Whoever controls himself when he desires, when he is terrified, when he craves, when he is angry, and when he is pleased, Allah will forbid his body from the Fire.

key_terms.النار: al-Nar -- the Hellfire; eschatological punishment from which self-control provides protection
key_terms.نفس: nafs -- the self or ego; in Islamic psychology, the lower self that must be disciplined through spiritual effort

ai.seo_question: What five emotional states must a Muslim control according to Imam al-Sadiq to be protected from Hellfire?
ai.summary: Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that mastery over the self (nafs) in five emotional states -- desire, fear, craving, anger, and pleasure -- earns divine protection from Hellfire. This hadith, recorded in a session on Friday the 26th of Rabi al-Awwal 368 AH, identifies self-control as the key to salvation, a theme central to Islamic ethics and the Quranic description of the righteous.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
